I bisected the regression to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/119987. cc @bruvzg

```
processed character with relative index 1, glyph flags 1, glyph index 69, origin (556.2812, 330.5)
processed character with relative index 2, glyph flags 1, glyph index 70, origin (566.25, 330.5)
```

```
processed character with relative index 2, glyph flags 44, glyph index 0, origin (603.3438, 330.5)
processed character with relative index 3, glyph flags 41, glyph index 0, origin (603.3438, 330.5)

processed character with relative index 2, glyph flags 1, glyph index 73, origin (597.5469, 330.5)
processed character with relative index 2, glyph flags 44, glyph index 0, origin (603.3438, 330.5)
processed character with relative index 3, glyph flags 41, glyph index 0, origin (603.3438, 330.5)
```

This is normal behavior. In general, you should never expect number of glyph to match number of characters, it is not true for any complex script (even for basic Latin, some characters can be replaced with ligatures), and "virtual glyphs" (glyphs that do not correspond to any character in the source text) can be inserted in multiple conditions (usually for internal processing purpose like alignment and line breaking). Draw and FX calls can also be called multiple times for the same glyph (with different offset), since some glyphs can be duplicated for alignment.

When drawing, you can always ignore glyphs with glyph index `0`, since these are non-visual (e.g, spaces), but not "virtual glyphs" (some can be drawn, e.g, kashidas used to align Arabic text).

If you need character indices in the original text that glyph correspond to, use `range` property of the `CharFXTransform`.

But I guess we probably should not call `_process_custom_fx` for "virtual glyphs" with zero index, since it these won't be useful.

And documentation should be probably updated, current one does not tell anything about the way `_process_custom_fx` called and difference between glyphs and characters.

Ok, I think I see what you mean. The ``range`` gives the first character that a glyph corresponds to (inclusive) and the last character that it corresponds to (exclusive), correct?  But in my example project if I add a line to report the range, I get this (in 4.8.dev7):

```
processed character with relative index 0, glyph flags 1, glyph index 68, range (0, 1), origin (547.0, 330.5)
processed character with relative index 1, glyph flags 1, glyph index 69, range (1, 2), origin (556.2812, 330.5)
processed character with relative index 2, glyph flags 1, glyph index 70, range (2, 3), origin (566.25, 330.5)
processed character with relative index 0, glyph flags 1, glyph index 71, range (4, 5), origin (578.3594, 330.5)
processed character with relative index 1, glyph flags 1, glyph index 72, range (5, 6), origin (588.3281, 330.5)
processed character with relative index 2, glyph flags 1, glyph index 73, range (6, 7), origin (597.5469, 330.5)
processed character with relative index 3, glyph flags 41, glyph index 0, range (7, 8), origin (603.3438, 330.5)
```

The range of the last call to ``_process_custom_fx`` is (7, 8), and there is no 7th character in the original string. That still seems wrong to me. Or have I misunderstood?

The reason I'm interested in this is that I'm trying to implement an effect that changes the scale of the text. Scaling the text by calling ``Transform2D.scaled()`` by itself doesn't work right because the origin isn't in the right spot and the letters end up flying off the page. I need to call ``TextServer.font_get_glyph_size()`` and ``TextServer.font_get_glyph_offset()`` to be able to move the origin to the visual center of the glyph before I scale it, and calling those requires me to know the font size. But I couldn't find any way to get the font size in ``_process_custom_fx()`` other than checking what it was in the original string. 

The problem I was having that led me to file the bug was that these calls to ``_process_custom_fx()`` were looking for the font size of the character one past the end of the string, which didn't exist. If I use ``CharFXTransform.range.x`` instead of ``CharFXTransform.relative_index`` then I would still have that problem here because the last value still corresponds to a character that doesn't actually exist in the original string.

> The range of the last call to _process_custom_fx is (7, 8), and there is no 7th character in the original string. That still seems wrong to me. Or have I misunderstood?

This is indeed not ideal, RTL and Label are always adding zero width space to the last line (to match line break character at the end of other lines) and doing it before text processing, so it counts as s source string.

> I need to call TextServer.font_get_glyph_size() and TextServer.font_get_glyph_offset() to be able to move the origin to the visual center of the glyph before I scale it, and calling those requires me to know the font size. But I couldn't find any way to get the font size in _process_custom_fx() other than checking what it was in the original string.

Not sure why it is not passed, it would make sense to add font size to FX.

> Ok, I think I see what you mean. The range gives the first character that a glyph corresponds to (inclusive) and the last character that it corresponds to (exclusive), correct?

Yes.

It was said that the documentation should be updated. Is someone working on that? If not, I'd be willing to try to do it myself, although I'm not totally confident I understand the system well enough to avoid introducing some kind of new error. Here's a summary of what I would change (in ``https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/doc/classes/CharFXTransform.xml``).

- ``brief_description``
  - Say that the ``CharFXTransform`` operates on glyphs, rather than characters.
- ``description``
  - Briefly explain characters, glyphs, ligatures, text shaping, and how they relate to CharFXTransform.
  - Mention that ligatures can be disabled with ``[opentype_features="liga=0"][/opentype_features]``. I don't see a corresponding ``RichTextLabel.push_opentype_features()`` method or any other way to do this from a script, but if there is one I would mention that too. 
- Member ``glyph_count`` 
  - Briefly explain what grapheme clusters are. Maybe link to the Unicode standard for more information.
  - Write what the value of ``glyph_count`` is when the current glyph is not the first glyph in a cluster (seems to be zero).
- Member ``offset``
  - As far as I can tell, the value of ``offset`` is always ``(0, 0)`` by default and this is effectively a second transform applied before the ``transform``, with ``transform.origin`` being the actual default offset of the glyph. I would explicitly say that.
- Member ``outline``
  - It seems like when text is drawn with an outline, the ``RichTextEffect._process()`` method is first called once each for the outline of every glyph, with ``outline == true``. Then it's called once each for every glyph itself, with ``outline == false``. I would explicitly say that.
 - Member ``range``
   - Phrase this description as "Indices of the first (inclusive) and last (exclusive) characters corresponding to this glyph, relative to the beginning of the ``RichTextLabel``'s text."
 - Member ``relative_index``
   - Phrase this description as "Index of the first character corresponding to this glyph, relative to the beginning of the current custom ``RichTextEffect``."
 - Member ``transform``
   - Mention that the glyph's default offset is ``transform.origin`` and not in ``offset``. 
   - Mention that the ``origin`` is the offset from the top left corner of the label to the left side of the glyph's final position at the baseline.
   - Mention that in order to transform a glyph's scale or rotation successfully it's useful to call ``TextServer.font_get_glyph_size()``, and ``TextServer.font_get_glyph_offset()``, and how the resulting values should be used.
